attempts.summary: Configured node1 (OpenWrt) as the DHCP server on the private eth1 network shared with node2 and node3. Added a UCI network interface 'priv' (192.168.50.1/24 on eth1), a firewall zone 'priv' (input/output/forward ACCEPT) with forwarding to wan, and a dnsmasq DHCP pool (192.168.50.100-249) on that interface. Added a static DHCP host reservation binding node2's eth1 MAC to 192.168.50.50, so node2 always gets that same address; node3 is left unreserved and draws from the general pool. Verified node2 gets 192.168.50.50 across repeated lease renewals and node3 gets a distinct pool address. Made the DHCP-client config persistent on node2/node3 (Alpine /etc/network/interfaces + rc-update). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on node1, node2, and node3: captured pre-restart boot_id/uptime/service baselines, issued native `reboot`, polled until exec access returned, confirmed each node's boot_id changed and uptime reset to ~0, and verified post-restart recovery (node1's dnsmasq/firewall/priv-interface config and lease table intact; node2 auto-reacquired its reserved 192.168.50.50; node3 auto-reacquired a pool address).
